active_paradigms.idea: Hardcode the known best published packing structure for n=26 (from packomania/known-optimal databases) as starting centers, then polish with the existing SLSQP
active_paradigms.description: The current program generates candidate layouts from scratch via heuristic templates, which wastes most of its 350s budget rediscovering structure that is already known. Instead, embed the coordinates of the best-known 26-circle packing in the unit square (available from the Packomania literature / Erich Friedman's circle packing records, which list the optimal arrangement for maximizing the minimum radius; the AlphaEvolve 2.635 result also has published structure). Hardcode these 26 center positions as a high-precision constant array (and optionally several top alternative arrangements as additional seeds). Then run a single joint SLSQP polish (already implemented in the program as slsqp_polish) over centers and radii starting from these literature-exact seeds. Because these seeds are far closer to the global optimum than any heuristic layout, the local optimizer converges to a better basin. Optionally perturb each seed with a few small Gaussian jitters and polish each, keeping the best valid result.
active_paradigms.cautions: Coordinates from literature are for maximizing the MINIMUM radius; adapt by treating them as center seeds only. Verify the 26-point configuration actually fits in the unit square with the correct index ordering. Keep the final SLSQP polish to guarantee evaluator validity (tolerance 1e-6), and always return the best valid solution found, falling back to the current program's output if anything fails.

active_paradigms.idea: Global search via scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on center coordinates with LP-evaluated objective
active_paradigms.description: Replace the perturbation-restart loop (mini basin hopping with fixed sigmas) with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 52 center coordinates, using the existing compute_max_radii LP as the inner objective (sum of LP-optimal radii for given centers). Dual annealing combines simulated-annealing-style stochastic jumps with local L-BFGS refinement, giving much better global exploration than the current fixed-sigma jitter restarts. Parameterize centers directly with bounds [0.02, 0.98], set a visit parameter around 2.5 and acceptance around -5, and give it the full remaining time budget (~200s) with maxiter in the thousands. Warm-start from the current best arrangement so it can only improve. After annealing finishes, run the existing SLSQP joint polish on the best found centers to squeeze out the final digits.
active_paradigms.cautions: Dual annealing needs many objective evaluations; use the fast sparse-LP radius solver (compute_max_radii) inside the objective so each evaluation is cheap. Enforce bounds via clipping and always validate the final result against the evaluator's exact tolerance (1e-6) before returning. Budget iterations so total runtime stays well under 350s.

active_paradigms.idea: Structured parameterization + differential evolution over layout parameters with per-generation LP radii
active_paradigms.description: Run a population-based global optimizer over a reduced parameterization: instead of 52 free coordinates, parameterize each layout family (A-E) by a small set of continuous parameters (row spacing, stagger offsets, corner-circle positions, row counts as discrete choices) and let differential_evolution search that low-dimensional space, evaluating each candidate by placing centers and solving the LP for radii. The low dimension (5-10 parameters per family) makes differential evolution very effective, and the population maintains diverse structural candidates simultaneously. Use strategy 'best1bin', mutation (0.3, 1.0), crossover 0.7, population size ~15× dimension, and a time-bounded maxiter. Then take the top few distinct population members (deduplicated by structure), run the existing greedy refine + SLSQP polish on each, and return the best. This is fundamentally different from the current single-trajectory perturbation search because it explores multiple structural basins in parallel.
active_paradigms.cautions: Population × LP evaluations can be expensive; prune the LP constraint matrix aggressively (already done via border-distance pruning). Use polish='L-BFGS-B' sparingly since the objective is only piecewise smooth. Always validate the final packing with the evaluator's exact criteria and fall back to the incumbent best if any candidate is invalid.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct nonlinear optimization over centers+radii jointly with SLSQP, replacing the LP-for-fixed-centers decomposition
tried_paradigms.description: Reformulate the packing as a single direct nonlinear program: variables are all 52 centers and 26 radii (78 total). Objective: maximize sum of radii. Constraints (all smooth, exact): for each pair (i,j): (x_i-x_j)^2+(y_i-y_j)^2 >= (r_i+r_j)^2; for each circle and each wall: x_i-r_i>=0, 1-x_i-r_i>=0, same for y. Feed the current best solution (which scores 2.585) as the feasible warm start, so SLSQP starts from a valid point and can only improve. Unlike the current LP-on-fixed-centers approach (which restricts radii given frozen centers), this jointly moves centers and grows radii, escaping the fundamental limitation that the LP optimum is only optimal for the given positions. Run SLSQP with tolerance ~1e-10 and multiple restarts from perturbed feasible points within the time budget, keeping the best valid result. This directly attacks the gap: the current method's centers are only locally optimal under greedy axis-aligned moves, while SLSQP follows the true gradient of the joint problem.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The 1e-6 overlap tolerance must be respected — shrink radii by 1e-7 margin in the objective. SLSQP with 78 variables needs a feasible warm start; use the current best arrangement as the start. Keep iterations bounded (~200) to fit the timeout. Verify validity with the evaluator's exact checks before returning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Voronoi/power-diagram (Laguerre) fixed-point iteration for simultaneous repositioning
tried_paradigms.description: For fixed radii, the optimal center placement relates to the power diagram (Laguerre Voronoi): each circle should sit at the incenter-like point of its power cell clipped to the square. Use an iterative fixed-point scheme: given current radii, compute the clipped Voronoi/power diagram of the 26 sites (scipy.spatial.Voronoi, manually clipping cells against the four walls), move each center toward the point of its cell that maximizes its distance to cell boundaries (the Chebyshev center of the cell — computable via small LP per cell or via the cell's incenter), then recompute radii with the existing LP. This is a fundamentally different geometric dynamic than greedy coordinate descent: it moves all circles simultaneously to their geometrically natural positions, often converging in 10-30 iterations to configurations unreachable by axis-aligned single/pair moves. Initialize from the current best solution and from the top few layout candidates.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii via better global center placement; validity
tried_paradigms.cautions: Clip the Voronoi diagram to the unit square (use the half-plane representation of Voronoi ridges intersected with walls). Guard against degenerate cells (empty cells, vertices at infinity) by falling back to the previous iterate. Convergence can oscillate — damp with step factor 0.5 and keep the best-sum iterate rather than the last. Always recompute final radii with the existing LP (compute_max_radii) to guarantee validity.

tried_paradigms.idea: Known-structure template seeding: enumerate contact-graph topologies and solve radii by LP on the exact contact structure
tried_paradigms.description: The current program only tries 4 hand-designed layout templates. Instead, systematically enumerate plausible contact-structure templates: choose which circles touch which walls (corner circles touch 2 walls, edge circles 1, interior 0) and an adjacency graph consistent with a hexagonal-ish or mixed pattern. For each template, parametrize centers by the radii themselves: a circle touching the left wall has x=r; touching left and bottom has x=r, y=r; touching circle j and wall w gives one equation. This yields a system where positions are functions of radii, and maximizing sum of radii subject to the remaining non-overlap constraints becomes a small LP or least-squares fixed point. Concretely: generate templates by taking the known-best n=25 and n=27 packings' structure (documented in literature: n=26 optimal packings often derive from perturbing adjacent-n optima), plus asymmetric variants of the current layouts with 6 rows (e.g., 4,5,4,5,4,4 staggered), and rows of unequal spacing. Evaluate each template's radii via the existing LP and keep the best before a light polish. The key insight: the optimal n=26 packing is likely structurally asymmetric with several wall-bound large circles, which none of the current 4 templates capture well.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by finding a better structural basin than the 4 current templates
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep the total number of enumerated templates modest (a few hundred) so LP evaluation stays within the timeout. Some templates will produce degenerate LPs (infeasible contact patterns) — skip them gracefully. The final answer must still pass the evaluator's pairwise check with the 1e-6 tolerance; apply the small safety margin. Combine with the existing Powell polish only as a final single step on the best template result.

tried_paradigms.idea: Hard-code the known best n=26 packing structure with a fully-implicit contact-graph solve
tried_paradigms.description: The best known packings for n=26 in a square have published coordinates (e.g., from Friedman's 'Packing circles in squares' tables and the AlphaEvolve result). Instead of generating layouts from parametric families, encode the approximate known-best configuration (26 centers) as a constant array, then run ONE joint scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP or trust-constr) over all 78 variables with exact pairwise-distance and wall constraints to polish it to machine precision. The key difference from the current program: the starting point is a near-optimal topology (correct contact graph), so the optimizer only needs to converge to the exact optimum rather than discover the structure. The contact graph topology matters far more than the local search; the current program's lattice families likely have the wrong adjacency structure.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii (primary score), by starting from the structurally-correct arrangement
tried_paradigms.cautions: Coordinates must be scaled to the unit square; verify feasibility of the warm start by shrinking radii via the existing LP before optimization; keep the 1e-6 tolerance margin; only accept the polished result if it validates.

tried_paradigms.idea: Greedy sequential insertion with maximal-radius placement (maximin frontier growth)
tried_paradigms.description: Replace all layout families with a deterministic greedy: maintain a set of placed circles; at each step, enumerate candidate positions formed by (a) tangent to two existing circles, (b) tangent to one circle and one wall, (c) tangent to two walls (corners) — all computable in closed form. For each candidate position, compute the achievable radius (LP or direct formula), and place the next circle at the candidate with the largest radius. This grows the packing from the four corners inward, naturally producing the mixed large-corner/small-interior radius distribution that beats uniform hex lattices. After all 26 are placed, run the existing LP radius assignment and one SLSQP polish pass. This is fundamentally different from lattice templates: the structure emerges from geometry rather than being imposed.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii via better topological structure (corner-heavy, wall-heavy arrangements)
tried_paradigms.cautions: Candidate enumeration is O(n^2) per step — fine for n=26; must clip candidates inside the square; deduplicate near-identical candidates; use a fixed deterministic tie-breaking rule so the constructor is reproducible; keep total runtime well under the 350s budget.

tried_paradigms.idea: Multi-start trust-constr global optimization with contact-graph topology search
tried_paradigms.description: The current SLSQP polish uses a single constraint Jacobian structure and fixed perturbation schedule. Instead, use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr' (which handles the 325 nonlinear inequality constraints more robustly via interior-point/interior barrier, and supports sparse Jacobians via scipy.sparse), run from ~20 diverse feasible starts: the 4 corners + hex interior family, the greedy-insertion result, and random perturbations of each. trust-constr's handling of many constraints and its barrier method tends to find better local optima than SLSQP on packing problems because it stays strictly feasible throughout, so no polish round can lose the best solution. Keep the best valid result across all starts. This replaces the brittle SLSQP+perturbation alternation with a proper globalized nonlinear program.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by escaping the shallow local optimum the current SLSQP polish is stuck in
tried_paradigms.cautions: trust-constr is slower per iteration — budget starts carefully (e.g., maxiter=300 each); always keep the incumbent best feasible solution; use the sparse constraint Jacobian pattern (LinearConstraint for walls, NonlinearConstraint with sparse jac for pairs); validate every candidate before accepting.
